name: Thesys C1 (now OpenUI Cloud) and OpenUI
tagline: Hosted generative-UI API plus open compact UI language

license.notes: OpenUI (framework, OpenUI Lang, renderers) is MIT. C1 / OpenUI Cloud and OpenUI Gateway are proprietary hosted services.

adoption.summary: Commercial generative-UI API rebranded as OpenUI Cloud, with an open-source OpenUI framework that is growing quickly (10.5k stars).

maintainability.summary: Active open-source repo backed by a commercial product.

architecture.summary: C1 was an OpenAI-compatible LLM API that returns UI (charts, forms, tables, cards) instead of text, rendered by Thesys's React SDK. It is now 'OpenUI Cloud', built on the open OpenUI framework: developers define a component library (Zod-typed), generate a system prompt from it, the model streams OpenUI Lang (a compact text language, not JSON), and React/Vue/Svelte/Angular renderers draw it progressively. @openuidev/a2ui offers an A2UI v1.0 client with OpenUI Lang component payloads; @openuidev/langchain streams OpenUI through AG-UI.
key_points: OpenUI Lang: compact, streaming-first, claims up to 67% fewer tokens than JSON formats
Library-driven prompts and controlled rendering (only registered components)
Hosted extras: validation/correction/fallback, gateway across models, observability

claims.text: OpenUI Lang uses 55-67% fewer tokens than Vercel json-render and Thesys C1 JSON across seven scenarios (tiktoken, GPT-5 encoder)
3x faster renders compared to JSON renderers

performance.summary: Token benchmark is published in the repo (reproducible); render-speed and user-preference claims are marketing without published method.

agent_usability.how: Generation API/SDK: the model outputs UI as OpenUI Lang (or C1 responses) that a client renders; no live control channel.
agent_usability.integration_effort: Low for web apps: swap the LLM endpoint (C1) or add the OpenUI renderer and prompt.
agent_usability.readback: Not documented beyond normal chat/app state (not verified).
agent_usability.granular_edits: Not documented; responses are regenerated per turn (not verified).
agent_usability.summary: Optimised for cheap, fast generation of web UI, not for operating a live interface.

score_notes.ui_as_data: OpenUI Lang is a serializable text format, but not JSON.
score_notes.agent_drivable: More than code generation (constrained DSL rendered safely) but no protocol to change a live instance.
score_notes.readback: No readback mechanism found in docs reviewed.

steelman: Thesys attacks the real cost of generative UI: tokens and latency. OpenUI Lang is a purpose-built compact language that, by its own reproducible tiktoken benchmark, needs roughly half to a third of the tokens of json-render or C1's own old JSON, which means faster first paint and cheaper turns. The framework is MIT, renders in four web frameworks, interoperates with A2UI and AG-UI, and the hosted OpenUI Cloud adds the unglamorous production parts (validation, correction, fallbacks, model gateway, observability) teams otherwise build themselves.
weaknesses: C1 itself is a proprietary SaaS; the brand has shifted (C1 -> OpenUI Cloud), so 'C1' docs and APIs may move
Another UI dialect (OpenUI Lang) beside A2UI and json-render
No readback, patching or history for agents (not documented)
Customer list and performance claims beyond the token benchmark are marketing

relation_to_scene.overlap: Agent-generated UI constrained to a trusted component library.
relation_to_scene.scene_reinvents: Little; scene does not target model-generated UI token cost.
borrow: A compact text form for agent-written scenes to cut tokens (the token benchmark is a useful yardstick)
Prompt generation from the component library
relation_to_scene.gap_left: Terminal rendering, live control, readback, data streams bypassing the model, pixels, history.
relation_to_scene.verdict_why: A web generation service; only its compact-language token-cost lesson applies to scene.
